environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, MSVC 19.51, GNS 1.6.1 and OpenSSL 3.6.5 via vcpkg 65a2c23, loopback, one process, real time, 1 ms loop
game_exe_sha256: N/A (prototype does not touch the game)
objective: KI-35, review #38 (FB-38-02): how much of the harsh tail (reconnects over 3 s) is time inside the DTLS cookie exchange, and how much of it is spent retransmitting the first ClientHello before the HelloVerifyRequest arrives? Measurement only: every batch runs today's default (timer 250 ms doubling to 1 s, cookie on, max_new_handshakes_per_s 64, confirm_binding off). No default, behaviour or gate change.
hypothesis: Predeclared (e5eb82f, before any tooling or run; Codex passes 1-3 fixed the attempt split, pass 4 approved). Per backend on harsh: S = attributable reconnects with total > 3000 ms; primary R_wait = share of S with total - cookie_wait <= 3000, exact 95% Wilson interval; lower bound >= 0.25 'explain part of the tail', upper bound < 0.25 'do not explain the tail', otherwise 'inconclusive'; |S| < 30 or more than 10% unattributable 'not assessable'; chi-square (df 3) across the 4 harsh batches on P(total > 3 s) and P(hello0_tx >= 2), p < 0.01 'heterogeneous'. GNS harsh decides: explain -> predeclare a behavioural cookie experiment; do not explain -> return to GNS establishment; otherwise the owner and reviewer choose. R_cookie, R per phase, R_wait with 0 restarts, phases in and outside S, flight classes and the slow profile are reported only. R_wait is an accounting ceiling, not a prediction.
procedure: Tooling on 1d56b6b (Codex approved on its second pass; 13 self-tests): tools/ki35/reconnect_probe.cpp splits the client's ClientHellos after t0 into handshake attempts (boundaries inner_connected, inner_disconnected, rejected; a new peer id also starts one), takes the final attempt's attempt_hello, last_hello0, cookie_hello, auth and hello0_tx, and counts the host's message_seq 0 ClientHello receptions and HVRs within [attempt_hello, cookie_hello] from the len=/seq= header trace (no payload); tools/ki35/run_cookie_probe.py applies the rules; run_reconnect_probe.homogeneity_p gained the df 3 closed form. 12 batches of 100 cycles: harsh (15% loss, 5% duplicates, 80 + U[0,40] ms) UDP seeds 4901-4904 and GNS repetitions 1-4; slow (150 + U[0,50] ms, 1% loss) UDP 4905-4906 and GNS 5-6. Attempt 1 (ki35-cookie-2026-10-28-143330-1d56b6b, tooling identical) stopped and is kept unjudged: 7 harsh batches complete, gns-4-off-harsh exited 4 after 24 cycles (cycle 22 timed out with a mean loop iteration of about 1317 s, so the process made almost no progress for about 22 min; cycle 23 failed with reconnect_window_expired with a mean iteration of about 21 s) and the runner ended at 16:59:50, 4 s into udp-4905-off-slow; Windows logged low virtual memory from 16:58, with another python.exe (not the runner) near 100 GB; the runner's own cause of death is not established. Attempt 2 ran on 2c193b8 (clean; tools identical to 1d56b6b) from 06:39 to 09:26 on 2026-10-29, as a process detached through WMI, watched for completion, stop, stall and free virtual memory below 4 GB; no low-memory event was logged during it.
expected_result: If GNS harsh explains part of the tail, a separately predeclared behavioural experiment on the exchange (verification, stateless gate and budget kept); if not, KI-35 returns to GNS establishment; if inconclusive, no behavioural cookie experiment follows from this evidence alone.
observed_result: Complete (12/12 batches, exit 0, 1200 cycles): 800 harsh and 400 slow reconnects, 0 timeouts, 0 failures, 0 that never started, 0 unattributable, 0 restarts (attempts > 1) in any batch; --analyze reproduces verdict.json identically. Homogeneity held: UDP p 0.273 (over 3 s) and 0.018 (hello0 resent), GNS 0.155 and 0.971. P(total > 3 s): UDP 30/400, GNS 118/400. Primary R_wait: UDP 8/30 = 0.267 [0.142, 0.444], GNS 23/118 = 0.195 [0.134, 0.276]: both 'inconclusive' (GNS upper bound 0.276 is above 0.25, lower bound below). Reading by the predeclared rule: inconclusive; the owner and reviewer choose. Reported only, GNS harsh S (n 118): R_cookie 46/118 = 0.39 [0.31, 0.48]; R_notice 0.22 [0.16, 0.30], R_establish 0.68 [0.59, 0.76], R_handshake 0.64 [0.55, 0.72], R_session 0.55 [0.46, 0.64]; largest phase in S: establish 48, session 32, handshake 29, cookie 9, notice 0; phase p50 in S (ms): notice 196, establish 1094, cookie 225, handshake 848, session 712, against 199 / 399 / 193 / 572 / 211 outside S. UDP harsh S (n 30): R_cookie 12/30 = 0.40; largest phase handshake 22, session 6, cookie 2. Harsh, both backends: the first ClientHello was resent in 27% (UDP 108/400) and 30% (GNS 118/400) of reconnects; mean hello0_tx 1.34 / 1.39, max 5; cookie_wait p50 0, p95 720 (both), p99 722 (UDP) / 1706 (GNS) ms. Slow: every reconnect sent the first ClientHello twice (hello0_tx = 2 in 200/200 on each backend), the second about 236 ms after the first, and the cookie ClientHello followed it by a median of 99-121 ms per batch: in 389/400 by less than 300 ms (the minimum RTT), which fits an answer to the first ClientHello, and in 11/400 by 313-391 ms, which fits an answer to the resend; P(total > 3 s) UDP 1/200, GNS 43/200 (GNS R_wait 36/43, reported only). Secondary replication on EXP-047's off harsh batches (cookie measured from first_hello): GNS R_cookie 37/92 = 0.40 [0.31, 0.50], UDP 10/19 = 0.53 [0.32, 0.73]; cookie p50 / p95 / p99 GNS 195 / 906 / 3843 ms, UDP 210 / 923 / 956.
errors: The experiment ran as predeclared; only attempt 2 is judged. The primary reading is inconclusive on both backends: removing the time lost to unanswered first ClientHellos would bring at most 13-28% of GNS harsh reconnects over 3 s under the limit (95%), so neither 'explains' nor 'does not explain' holds at the 0.25 threshold. R_wait and every R per phase are accounting ceilings that assume the rest of the reconnect would not change; they overlap and do not add up, and they are not predictions of any change. The flight classes are approximate: the host's receptions are counted only up to the client's cookie_hello, so a retransmitted ClientHello still in flight then is not counted. On slow, 393/400 reconnects read 'hello_lost' at 1% loss. In 367 of them the cookie ClientHello left less than 150 ms (the minimum one-way delay) after the resend, so the resend could not have been counted and the class is an artifact of the window; the other 26 (resend-to-cookie 150-300 ms in 20, over 300 ms in 6) cannot be told apart from real loss, and 7 reconnects did count both ClientHellos. Separately, for response attribution: in the 389/400 whose cookie ClientHello came less than one minimum RTT (300 ms) after the resend, the timing fits an answer to the first ClientHello, so the resend was most likely spurious; the 11 others fit an answer to the resend. The harsh 'hello_lost' share is affected the same way to an unknown degree. The slow observation (the 250 ms initial timer fired before the answer in every reconnect, and the resend was most likely spurious in 389/400) is descriptive input to FB-38-03, not a test of it. The secondary replication was computed while building the tooling, after the predeclaration commit; it is reported only and was not used to set any rule. No restart was seen, but restarts are a lower bound by construction. One process, loopback, simulated impairment; GNS loss is not seedable. KI-35 is not fixed.
follow_up: No default change and no behavioural cookie experiment follows from this result alone. Reported only and not a rule: on GNS harsh the establish phase is the largest phase most often among reconnects over 3 s (48/118) and has the largest ceiling (0.68), which is consistent with FB-38-02's alternative (GNS establishment). The owner and the reviewer choose between: GNS establishment (EXP-036/041), a cookie-retransmission change predeclared on its own (its ceiling is 0.13-0.28 on GNS), or the RTT-adaptive initial timer (FB-38-03, deferred), for which the slow profile shows a first-ClientHello resend in every reconnect, most likely spurious in 389/400. Any adoption is an owner decision followed by the soak gate.
